papers.title: Neurofeedback for Management of Musculoskeletal Pain: A Randomized Control Trial Using DOMS.
papers.abstract: Chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) pain is associated with maladaptive neuroplasticity, often reflected in altered alpha activity (8-13 Hz). Neurofeedback may offer a way to modulate this activity, yet most protocols target alpha activity during rest, despite movement being a common pain trigger. This study investigated whether neurofeedback during movement could modulate alpha activity and reduce pain in healthy individuals experiencing induced pain via delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS). This experiment was a randomized, two-armed, parallel-group trial. Twenty-nine participants were included (15 females, mean age = 28 years). Exclusions included neurological, psychiatric, MSK conditions. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (aiming to reduce alpha activity) or a control group (aiming to increase it). Alpha activity was assessed as the alpha power during rest and movement. DOMS was induced using eccentric exercise of muscle extensor carpi radialis in Session 1. Neurofeedback was administered in Session 2, where participants underwent three blocks of neurofeedback training, using individualized EEG-based visual feedback to modulate alpha activity. Session 3 assessed potential lasting neurofeedback effects. Pain was rated across the three sessions, which took place 24-48 h apart. DOMS induction was confirmed by increased pain (p < 0.001, r = 0.82) and reduced alpha activity during movement (p = 0.017, r = 0.49). Neurofeedback did not significantly alter alpha activity (p = 0.114, W = 0.05 for the control group, p = 0.338, W = 0.037 for the intervention group). A single neurofeedback session was insufficient to modulate brain activity or pain perception. Methodological factors, including limited training duration and participants' strategies, may have contributed to the lack of an observable effect. Although neurofeedback did not result in significant changes after one session, the observed alpha modulation following DOMS highlights the relevance of targeting neuroplasticity during MSK pain. Future studies should optimize training protocols and consider multisession designs to enhance clinical applicability.

papers.title: Clinical and Longitudinal Heterogeneity Within the Acute Outer Retinopathy Spectrum: A Three-Case Series.
papers.abstract: To describe three distinct presentations within the acute outer retinopathy (AOR) spectrum, emphasizing differences in stage, longitudinal evolution, and structure-function relationships. Retrospective case series. The first, a 14-year-old asymptomatic male, had bilateral sectoral and spot-like outer retinal lesions in the subacute-chronic stage. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrated outer nuclear layer thinning with ellipsoid and interdigitation zone disruption and focal retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) attenuation, without the angular sign of Henle fiber layer hyperreflectivity (ASHH). Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) revealed lesions with a hypoautofluorescent core and hyperautofluorescent border, while fluorescein angiography (FA) showed window-defect hyperfluorescence and focal venular wall staining. The second, a 20-year-old male, developed severe visual field loss after a viral illness. FAF showed perivenular outer retinal involvement, and OCT revealed perivenular disruption with ASHH documented at 11 months. Visual field deficits were severe and partially correlated with structural abnormalities, with incomplete recovery over 3 years. Pattern electroretinography showed borderline reduction, whereas full-field electroretinography was within the lower limits of normal. The third, a 43-year-old female, presented with acute visual symptoms and mild intraocular inflammation. FAF showed sectoral peripapillary hyperautofluorescence, with corresponding outer retinal disruption on OCT. FA demonstrated venular wall staining and optic disc hyperfluorescence without diffuse vascular leakage. Perimetry showed bilateral diffuse sensitivity loss, while electrophysiology demonstrated generalized cone-predominant photoreceptor dysfunction. These cases illustrate clinical and longitudinal heterogeneity within established AOR patterns, including asymptomatic subacute-chronic disease, perivenular disease with structure-function dissociation and late documentation of ASHH, and symptomatic sectoral disease with diffuse photoreceptor dysfunction.

papers.title: Early neurocognitive outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation.
papers.abstract: Characterization of early neuropsychological outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RFTHC) is essential to guide patient expectations around return to work, study, and caregiving. The current study aimed to describe the early neurocognitive sequelae of SEEG. Consecutive patients undergoing SEEG were prospectively recruited from two tertiary epilepsy centers in Melbourne, Australia. Patients were administered the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS) via telehealth before and 3 weeks after SEEG (M = 19.69 days, SD = 4.41). Given the telehealth platform, the coding subtest was substituted for the Symbol Digit Modalities Test, and a modified score of global cognitive function was calculated. To evaluate group changes, paired sample t-tests were performed. Reliable change indices were computed to explore individual-level changes. Pearson's correlation coefficients evaluated relationships between change in global cognitive function and SEEG admission variables. SEEG patients were invited to complete a semi-structured interview canvassing the recovery following SEEG. Twenty-eight patients completed the neuropsychological examination (M = 37.89 years, SD = 9.72, range = 17-56 years, 54% female). All patients underwent RFTHC with a mean of 11.43 (SD = 6.87, range = 2-28) coagulation sites. At a whole group level, 3-weeks post SEEG there was no evidence for global nor domain-specific cognitive change. Reliable change indices with 90% confidence revealed only 4% (1/28) declined on at least two measures and 10% (3/28) showed psychometric improvement. Pearson's correlational coefficients showed no evidence for association between change in global cognitive function with SEEG factors including admission length, number of spontaneous or stimulated seizures, number of electrodes, or number of RFTHC sites. Subjective reports of language change tended to be accompanied by a decline on the RBANS language index that did not meet reliable change criteria. Most patients reported returning to work around 4 weeks post SEEG. By 3 weeks, gross cognitive functioning tends to be in keeping with pre-SEEG performances for most patients. These findings have direct clinical implications for SEEG neuropsychological counseling. SEEG is increasingly used to guide epilepsy surgery. Despite this, little is known about the cognitive recovery in the weeks following the procedure. We found that for most patients, broad cognitive functioning 3 weeks after SEEG with coagulation was consistent with function before SEEG, with only a small minority showing significant changes. Some people who reported language difficulties also showed a decline on language testing, although this was often small. Of those patients working before SEEG, most returned to work by 4 weeks. These results provide important evidence to guide patient counseling, recovery planning, and management after SEEG.

papers.title: Validation of the diagnosis of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome: Challenges and lessons learned.
papers.abstract: Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by multiple seizure types, cognitive impairment, and distinct electroencephalographic (EEG) findings. However, evolving diagnostic criteria, heterogeneous clinical features, and inconsistent electronic health record (EHR) documentation complicate accurate diagnosis and cohort identification. As part of a Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute-sponsored study developing EHR-based computable phenotypes for LGS, we established a reference standard through retrospective chart review and epileptologist classification. A multicenter retrospective chart review was conducted across seven pediatric epilepsy centers. Stratified sampling using PCORnet data selected patients based on the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision diagnosis code for LGS or other intractable epilepsy diagnoses between 2016 and 2022. Clinical teams abstracted seizure history, EEG findings, developmental status, and treatment history. Two epileptologists independently reviewed each case as classic LGS, pragmatic LGS, or not LGS. Discordant cases underwent adjudication by a senior epileptologist. Cases with incomplete or unclear data underwent repeat abstraction and review. Of 997 identified patients, 935 underwent classification after exclusions. Initial epileptologist disagreement occurred in 105 cases (11%, unweighted Cohen kappa = 82%). Following adjudication, 130 cases underwent reabstraction to retrieve additional EEG reports and clinical details. Rereview reclassified 67 cases initially considered "not LGS": 33 classic LGS, 12 pragmatic LGS, and 22 excluded for insufficient data. Key EHR challenges included inconsistent EEG reporting, incomplete seizure type characterization, fragmented documentation of cognitive impairment, unclear age at onset, and variable terminology across institutions and providers. Slow spike-and-wave EEG findings were the most frequently missing diagnostic element. Validating LGS diagnoses using EHR data is complex and resource intensive. Standardized terminology, structured documentation, and rigorous multicenter validation may improve diagnostic accuracy, research cohort identification, computable phenotype development, and longitudinal care for individuals with LGS. Our results highlight important operational lessons for multicenter rare epilepsy studies and underscore the need for improved diagnosis pathways and longitudinal care systems for those with LGS and their families.

papers.title: Analysis of Factors Influencing the Psychological State of Patients After Autologous Liver Transplantation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND The use of ex vivo liver resection and autologous liver transplantation (ELRA) for end-stage hepatic alveolar echinococcosis is gradually increasing, while postoperative psychological disorders in these patients remain underrecognized. We prespecified that longer pre-transplant waiting time, postoperative complications, and higher transfusion volume would be associated with worse anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbance at 1 month after ELRA. MATERIAL AND METHODS This single-center retrospective study enrolled 138 patients who underwent ELRA from 2020 to 2025. We collected demographic data, perioperative clinical indexes, and scores at baseline and 1 month postoperatively using the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Univariate analysis and multivariate linear regression were used to identify independent influencing factors. RESULTS Longer pre-transplant waiting time independently predicted worse scores across all psychological and sleep scales (all P<0.05). Prolonged anhepatic phase duration was specifically associated with higher PSQI scores (P<0.05). Intraoperative transfusion showed marginal but nonsignificant associations, and postoperative complications were significant only in univariate analysis. CONCLUSIONS Longer pre‑transplant waiting time is the core and most consistent risk factor for poor mental health after ELRA, while prolonged anhepatic phase is specifically linked to postoperative sleep disturbance. These findings support the implementation of targeted, stage-specific psychological interventions, especially during the pre-transplant waiting period, to improve mental health and quality of life in patients undergoing ELRA.

papers.title: Is Less More? Exploring the Visual Processes of Minimalist and Complex Photography Through Eye Tracking and EEG.
papers.abstract: In a world filled with an overwhelming amount of visual information, the clean and distinctive visual style of minimalist photography stands out. However, empirical research on how minimalist style affects visual cognition and psychological responses remains limited. The present study investigated the effects of photographic style (minimalist versus complex) on viewers' visual behavior, emotional responses, and brainwave state by conducting quantitative psychological experiments. Thirty participants viewed photographs in one of the two styles. Eye-tracking, consumer-grade electroencephalography (EEG), and subjective psychological assessment data were collected, enabling comprehensive evaluation of how the participants looked at, responded to, and emotionally engaged with the images. At the level of visual behavior, minimalism elicited significantly reduced number of fixations and saccades, but the duration of a single fixation is significantly longer, and the heatmap hotspots are highly concentrated, presenting a focused processing pattern of fewer but longer gazes. On a psychological level, minimalism evoked significantly less feeling of complexity and greater relaxation, although there was no significant difference in the aesthetics score between the two styles. In terms of brainwave state, viewing minimalist images resulted in significantly higher attention eSense levels, while the meditation eSense level did not show a significant difference. The results of this study therefore show that minimalist composition may influence the visual search pattern to be more focused, which is compatible with the tendency of simplified organization predicted by the principle of simplification. This study not only deepens the theoretical understanding of the psychological mechanisms of minimalist aesthetics, but also provides practical reference for visual communication and image creation of minimalist composition serving as an effective strategy for guiding the eyes toward the core subject.

papers.title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions.
papers.abstract: Corpus callosotomy is an established palliative operation for drug-resistant epilepsy dominated by drop attacks, and it is performed in three extents: anterior, usually of the anterior two-thirds; total, in one or two stages; and selective posterior, which preserves the genu and rostral body. Meta-analysis finds no difference between them in overall seizure reduction, a difference in drop attack control favoring the posterior approach, and a graded difference in disconnection syndrome, but there has never been a prospective head-to-head comparison, and the optimal extent of section remains undefined. A search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection identified 62 experimental studies in which the corpus callosum or another forebrain commissure was sectioned with an epilepsy-related outcome, spanning 1948-2026 across six species and every major seizure model. This literature is neither absent nor recent. What it has almost never done is vary the extent of section: the few studies that varied it took the laterality of kindling transfer or of interictal synchrony as the endpoint, never seizure control and never cognitive cost. No study compares the three extents against a common outcome; none models the selective posterior operation as it is defined clinically; none randomizes between extents; and none combines graded disconnection with time-locked bilateral electrophysiology, diffusion-based verification of the fibers divided, and a behavioral read-out in the same animals. The effect of section is also bidirectional: focal seizures may intensify through loss of transcallosal inhibition, and in the pentylenetetrazol model callosal section paradoxically facilitates convulsions, which limits chemoconvulsant preparations. The asymmetry between the clinical and experimental literatures is therefore one of method rather than of volume or attention: the two answered different questions, and the question the clinical field now asks requires a manipulation the experimental literature has never performed. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Surgeons can treat severe epilepsies by cutting the bundle of fibers that joins the two halves of the brain, but they do not agree on how much of it to cut. We searched three databases and found 62 animal studies of this operation going back to 1948. Almost none of them compared different amounts of cutting, and none looked at the newest version of the operation. Answering the surgeons' question will require a new kind of animal experiment rather than more reading of the old ones.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Quinolin-2-One-Indole Schiff Base Hybrids as Potential EGFR-Targeted Anticancer Agents Against Breast and Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: A series of new quinolin-2-one-indole Schiff base hybrids was designed, synthesized, and tested as potential anticancer agents targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor. The designed compounds were synthesized via a multistep synthetic route comprising phenylhydrazone formation, Fischer indole cyclization, Vilsmeier-Haack formylation, and subsequent Schiff base condensation. Structural elucidation was performed using IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and mass spectral analysis. In silico studies demonstrated that the synthesized compounds exhibited strong binding affinities to both wild-type (PDB ID: 1M17) and mutant EGFR (PDB ID: 4ZAU), as evidenced by favorable docking scores, with PYd2 showing the strongest interaction. Molecular dynamics simulations over 100 ns further confirmed that the PYd2-EGFR complexes remained stable, maintaining consistent protein-ligand contacts and exhibiting stable RMSD and RMSF values throughout the simulation period. Predicted ADME-toxicity profiles demonstrated favorable drug-like properties, oral absorption, and acceptable toxicity profiles for most synthesized derivatives. In vitro anticancer evaluation against MDA-MB-231 and SK-OV-3 cell lines identified PYd2 as the most potent analog. ELISA-based studies demonstrated significant inhibition of EGFR expression and phosphorylation, while DAPI staining revealed characteristic apoptotic nuclear changes in treated cells. Overall, PYd2 showed favorable predicted EGFR binding and antiproliferative activity against both cancer cell lines.

papers.title: Tirzepatide for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Trial Evidence, Cardiometabolic Effects, and Implications for Cardiovascular Practice.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea affects approximately one billion adults worldwide and is associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. Obesity is its dominant reversible cause, yet positive airway pressure therapy splints the pharyngeal airway without addressing the adiposity that narrows it, and randomized trials have not shown that it reduces cardiovascular events. In December 2024, the United States Food and Drug Administration approved tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, as the first drug for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. We summarize the pharmacology of tirzepatide and the anatomic basis by which weight reduction improves upper airway patency, notably reduction of tongue and parapharyngeal fat. We then review the SURMOUNT-OSA program: two parallel 52-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolling 469 adults with obesity and an apnea-hypopnea index of at least 15 events per hour, one conducted without positive airway pressure and one during established positive airway pressure use. Tirzepatide reduced the apnea-hypopnea index by an estimated 20.0 and 23.8 events per hour relative to placebo, with concurrent reductions in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, systolic blood pressure, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein.

papers.title: Mapping mental health complexity in esports: an exploratory psychosocial network approach.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise in popularity of esports has brought increased attention to the unique mental health challenges faced by esports players, yet research in this area remains in its infancy. Early research suggests a substantial mental health burden and has examined associations between esports-specific stressors, mental health, and sleep disturbances. However, much of this work has relied on traditional methodologies, providing limited insight into how affective, psychosocial, sleep-related, and esports-specific indicators are organised within this competitive performance environment. To address this gap, we developed a bespoke 17-item questionnaire tailored for Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) network analysis, an exploratory approach for mapping the conditional dependency structure of complex multivariate systems such as mental health. A total of 1025 esports players from over 60 countries completed the survey. Game-related thought preoccupation, a core feature of gaming disorder, emerged as the most robust structural sink node, downstream of several psychosocial indicators, raising the hypothesis that it represents a compound indicator of broader upstream psychosocial strain. Depressed mood occupied an upstream position within the network, an observation that held more robustly for the psychopathological subnetwork as a whole than for depressed mood as the single source. Mental fatigue occupied an intermediate, connecting position between affective variables and the sleep and fatigue indicators. Its high prevalence, together with a positioning upstream of the sleep indicators, suggests that it may warrant closer examination in future research on training load, recovery, and sleep in esports, though this ordering rested on edges with moderate directional support. Emotion control and a sense of autonomy appeared to connect upstream affective distress with downstream esports-specific indicators such as esports-related stress, though was the least stable of the structural features identified. Collectively, these findings provide an exploratory map of how mental health-relevant indicators were organised in this performance environment, and generate concrete, testable hypotheses for future longitudinal, experimental, and intervention research.
keywords: Bayesian network; Depression; Directed Acyclic Graph; Emotion regulation; Esports; Game preoccupation; Mental fatigue; Mental health; Psychosocial network analysis; Sleep

papers.title: Childhood-onset parkinsonism, dystonia and severe muscle wasting in a Sudanese girl caused by a novel homozygous DnaJ heat shock protein family (heat shock protein 40) member C6 frameshift variant, with an incidental pathogenic breast cancer 1 gene secondary finding: a case report.
papers.abstract: DNAJC6-related juvenile parkinsonism is a rare autosomal recessive disorder of auxilin, a co-chaperone essential for clathrin-mediated synaptic vesicle recycling. Fewer than 50 kindreds have been reported worldwide, and the condition is easily missed when first-line investigations come back normal. We describe a Sudanese adolescent in whom a previously unreported homozygous DNAJC6 frameshift variant was identified only after a prolonged diagnostic journey that included a period during which her illness was mistakenly attributed to a functional neurological disorder. Clinical whole-exome sequencing additionally returned an incidental medically actionable BRCA1 secondary finding. A 13-year-old Sudanese girl, the eldest child of first-cousin parents, was born preterm and ventilated neonatally for severe respiratory distress. Her development was normal until age five, when an isolated upper-limb tremor first appeared. Over the next 8 years her condition progressed into severe juvenile parkinsonism: bilateral rest-and-action tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, generalized dystonia with prominent oromandibular involvement, dysphagia, profound cachexia, cognitive and behavioral decline, sleep and autonomic disturbance, episodic oculogyric crises and three discrete seizures. By approximately 11 she was wheelchair-dependent. Earlier, unrevealing investigations had led to a psychiatric diagnosis of functional neurological disorder, and the dopamine antagonists prescribed on that basis worsened her condition. Whole-exome sequencing later identified a novel homozygous DNAJC6 frameshift deletion (NM_001256864.2:c.1480del; p.Glu494ArgfsTer12), absent from population databases, alongside a heterozygous pathogenic BRCA1 deletion reported as an actionable secondary finding. Levodopa produced partial motor benefit, complicated by on-state dyskinesias, visual hallucinations and excessive daytime somnolence. Subsequent up-titration of carbidopa/levodopa to approximately 5-hourly dosing produced a further, clinically evident improvement in gait and fine-motor function. This case adds a previously unreported allele to the DNAJC6 catalog and characterizes the severe end of its phenotype, where corticospinal signs and life-threatening cachexia accompany the more familiar extrapyramidal features. It illustrates the harm that follows premature labeling of a progressive organic movement disorder as functional, especially when dopamine antagonists are then prescribed. The accompanying pathogenic BRCA1 secondary finding shows the dual diagnostic yield that clinical whole-exome sequencing can deliver. Early genetic investigation in childhood-onset movement disorders, particularly with consanguinity, should be the rule, and cascade pathways for actionable secondary findings embedded in routine practice.

papers.title: Circadian clock and its potential as a therapy for ischemic heart disease.
papers.abstract: According to an epidemiological survey, myocardial infarction, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and aortic rupture usually occur in the morning and summer and are characterized by more severe symptoms and poorer prognosis. The occurrence, development, treatment difficulties, and poor prognosis of ischemic heart disease are closely related to circadian rhythm disorders and the abnormal transcription of circadian clock genes. Normal circadian rhythms regulate neurohumoral regulation and energy metabolism, thereby playing a protective or modulatory role in ischemic heart disease (IHD). HIF1α links the IHD and circadian signaling pathways through the hypoxia response element (HRE) and Per-Arnt-Sim (PAS) domains in gene promoters and enhancers.

papers.title: Frailty transitions and the risk of multisystem burden of chronic disease: a prospective cohort study in China.
papers.abstract: Frailty, defined by a decline in physiological reserve, is a key determinant of adverse health outcomes in older populations. While baseline frailty has been shown to predict the development of chronic diseases, the impact of changes in frailty status over time, particularly in rapidly ageing populations like China, remains poorly understood. This study aimed to assess how baseline frailty and its longitudinal transitions influence the incidence of chronic diseases across multiple organ systems. We analysed data from 17,708 adults (aged ≥ 40) in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) collected between 2011 and 2018. Frailty was assessed using the Rockwood Frailty Index at baseline and at two-year follow-up, categorised as stable, improved, or worsened. We applied Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the onset of 13 major chronic diseases spanning cardiovascular, metabolic, respiratory, neurological, psychiatric, digestive, renal, and musculoskeletal systems. The study included 9,807 to 16,882 participants across 13 disease-specific subgroups, with a median follow-up period of 6.2-6.8 years for baseline frailty status and 4.4-5.0 years for frailty transitions. Frail individuals were typically older, more likely to be female, unmarried, with lower education, higher BMI, and reported fewer hours of sleep. Baseline frailty was associated with significantly higher risks for all 13 chronic diseases, with the strongest association observed for psychiatric problems (HR 5.17, 95% CI 3.24-8.24). Worsening frailty over time was linked to elevated risks, particularly for asthma (HR 3.91, 95% CI 1.28-11.91), while improvements in frailty showed reduced risks, notably for kidney diseases (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.22-0.63). The association was particularly strong in adults aged 40-65 years, indicating greater potential for risk modification in midlife. Frailty is a dynamic and modifiable predictor of multisystem chronic disease risk. Changes in frailty status offer valuable insights into future disease development, especially among middle-aged adults. Routine frailty monitoring in clinical settings may offer a strategic opportunity to delay or prevent the onset of chronic diseases through timely interventions. These findings emphasize the need for incorporating frailty-targeted strategies into public health and clinical care policies to enhance ageing-related disease prevention.
papers.journal: Archives of public health = Archives belges de sante publique

papers.title: Shivering, sweating and struggling: a qualitative study exploring the relationship between energy poverty and mental wellbeing across three European cities.
papers.abstract: The inability to meet energy needs, referred to as energy poverty, impacts mental wellbeing, hindering people's capacity to cope with the challenges that emerged from this constraint. Qualitative research on the relationship between energy poverty and mental wellbeing is limited and has primarily been conducted in the United Kingdom. This study aimed to explore this relationship in three European cities with distinct climates, societal characteristics and governance arrangements. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with individuals experiencing energy poverty in Leeds (United Kingdom), Heerlen (the Netherlands) and Valencia (Spain). Thematic analysis was guided by the Conceptual Framework for Public Mental Health. Interviews with 36 participants across Leeds, Valencia, and Heerlen revealed largely similar experiences linking energy poverty to mental wellbeing. Participants described persistent fear and worry about energy costs, thermal discomfort affecting mood and sleep, reduced agency over living conditions, and housing constraints shaping family relationships and social interactions. Experiences with public authorities further influenced wellbeing, with feelings of being acknowledged or overlooked emerging as key determinants. Although some contextual differences were observed, particularly related to climate, the pathways through which energy poverty affected mental wellbeing were consistent across the three cities. The consistency of experiences across three European cities suggests that the mental‑health impacts of energy poverty are systemic rather than context‑specific. Our findings underscore the need for multilevel interventions that address the complex determinants of mental wellbeing within energy‑poor populations, operating simultaneously at the individual, family, and community and structural levels. We call upon the public health field to engage in this issue, to protect and advocate for the mental wellbeing of people experiencing energy poverty, as society transitions to a low-carbon future.

papers.title: Longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and their association with cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity risk in postmenopausal women: evidence from the CHARLS study.
papers.abstract: To investigate the association between longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and the risk of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM) in a population of postmenopausal women. A total of 2,859 postmenopausal women from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were included, with 4 repeated measurements of night sleep duration collected from 2011 to 2018. Group-based trajectory modeling was adopted to identify distinct sleep duration trajectory patterns. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between sleep trajectories and incident CRMM ascertained between 2018 and 2020. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to validate the robustness of the findings. Three sleep duration trajectory patterns were identified: normal-stable (33.9% of the cohort), normal-fluctuating decline (52.0%), and short-rapid decline (14.1%). During a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome (incident CRMM) occurred in 108 participants (3.8%). Compared with normal-stable group, those in normal-fluctuating decline and short-rapid decline groups had an increased risk of CRMM (ORs of 2.30 [95%CI, 1.35-3.91] and 3.75 [95%CI, 1.99-7.07], respectively) after adjustment for multiple covariates. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these associations, which were independent of key baseline characteristics and missing data. In postmenopausal women, short and declining sleep duration trajectories are strong, independent risk factors for CRMM. Public health and clinical interventions should prioritize maintaining stable, adequate sleep to mitigate multimorbidity risk in this population.

papers.title: Associations between gastrointestinal symptoms and coexisting symptoms amongst patients in a palliative care unit: a PCOC-based longitudinal study.
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms are both common and distressing in patients receiving palliative care, however their relationships with coexisting symptoms and clinical factors, including functional status, clinician-rated problem severity, and palliative care phase, remain unclear in hospice ward settings. The Palliative Care Outcomes Collaboration (PCOC) framework enables for standardized daily symptom assessment and longitudinal evaluation. This study aimed to longitudinally investigate the associations between GI symptoms and related symptoms and clinical domains among patients admitted to a hospice ward. This retrospective cohort study included 1,008 unique adult patients admitted to the hospice ward of a tertiary medical center in central Taiwan between March 1, 2021 and September 30, 2023. Each patient contributed one hospice ward admission course and was followed from admission until death or transfer to home hospice care. Routine daily PCOC assessments collected throughout the admission course were analyzed longitudinally as repeated measurements within patients. Patients younger than 18 years, those with missing identification information, or those with incomplete PCOC data were excluded. Separate generalized estimating equation (GEE) models were constructed for the appetite, nausea, and bowel domains of the Symptom Assessment Scale (SAS), adjusting for demographic, clinical, functional, and symptom-related variables. Subgroup analyses were performed for cancer and non-cancer patients. Amongst the 1,008 patients, the mean age was 68.0 years, with 59.1% being male, and 86.5% having cancer. At admission, mean SAS scores were 2.45 for appetite loss, 1.91 for bowel discomfort, and 0.69 for nausea, indicating that appetite loss was the most prominent GI symptom. Nausea was significantly associated with sleep disturbance, appetite loss, bowel discomfort, and pain, while older age was associated with lower nausea severity. Appetite loss was associated with sleep disturbance, nausea, bowel discomfort, fatigue, pain, greater clinician-rated "other" and family problems, as well as deteriorating phase; referral from the general ward was associated with lower appetite distress. Bowel discomfort was associated with appetite loss, nausea, breathlessness, fatigue, pain, higher clinician-rated "other" problems, and higher Australia-modified Karnofsky Performance Status (AKPS). Subgroup analyses showed that symptom associations were generally more extensive in cancer patients than in non-cancer patients, particularly for appetite loss and bowel discomfort. GI symptoms in hospice ward patients are closely linked to coexisting symptoms, functional status, clinician-rated problem severity, and palliative care phase, and should not be assessed in isolation. Daily standardized assessment using the PCOC framework may help support more individualized symptom management for palliative care patients.

papers.title: Real world clinical practice patterns in nocturnal GERD management: insights from nationwide RELIEF survey.
papers.abstract: Nocturnal symptoms of GERD interfere with daytime functioning, work, and social activities, thereby negatively affecting health-related quality of life. Therefore, the present survey aimed to evaluate the clinical practice patterns regarding the management of nocturnal GERD in India. A digital questionnaire-based nationwide RELIEF survey was conducted among health care practitioners (HCPs) with gastroenterology practice across India. Physicians voluntarily responded to the survey questionnaire consisting of 24 questions based on their clinical experience. Following the collection of completed questionnaires, data were reviewed and analyzed. Of the 500 HCPs who were approached, 498 completed the study. GERD contributed to > 30% of patient burden every month. According to 25.30% of HCPs, 21-30% of patients with GERD complain of nocturnal symptoms. The most common risk factors in patients with nocturnal GERD were late-night meals (67.67%), followed by smoking (51%), BMI > 25 kg/m2 (50.20%), and a high-fat diet (50.40%). Most HCPs (83%) relied on symptoms and medical history to diagnose nocturnal GERD. A single-dose proton pump inhibitor (PPI) regimen was the most preferred treatment, reported by 31.53% of HCPs, with esomeprazole preferred by 54% of physicians. Efficacy (58.03%), minimum or no drug-drug interactions (29.92%), and cost (22.49%) are the important aspects for choosing a PPI. HCPs (63.18%) opted for 4-8 weeks of PPI therapy to achieve resolution of nocturnal GERD symptoms, followed by 3-6 months of maintenance therapy (57.95%). Common causes of non-adherence to PPIs, as reported by 80.72% of HCPs, were stopping treatment once symptoms improved (53.01%), cost (39.56%), and incomplete disease awareness (29.92%). Most of the HCPs (42.77%) reported no side effects with the use of PPIs. The survey highlighted key insights into managing nocturnal GERD in India, with nearly one-fourth of GERD patients reporting nocturnal symptoms like heartburn and regurgitation, emphasizing the need for lifestyle modifications and suitable pharmacological interventions. The management strategy primarily includes PPI therapy, with esomeprazole being the preferred choice for nocturnal GERD.

papers.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
papers.abstract: Pharmacotherapy is recommended as the first-line treatment for adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), yet some individuals show partial or inadequate response associated with adverse effects. These limitations have prompted interest in adjunctive or alternative interventions. Electroencephalography (EEG) neurofeedback is a non-pharmacological intervention for ADHD, which enables self-regulation of neural activity. This systematic review synthesised clinical, cognitive, and electrophysiological outcomes of EEG neurofeedback in adult ADHD, and examined standard versus personalised training protocols. Following PRISMA guidelines, four databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, Ovid, Web of Science) were searched from 1960 to October 2025 for this PROSPERO-registered review (ID: CRD420251020898). Eligible studies included adults (≥ 18 years) with a formal ADHD diagnosis undergoing EEG neurofeedback. Outcomes comprised symptom severity, cognitive performance, electrophysiology, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I V2. Seven studies (three RCTs, four non-randomised; n = 390) met inclusion criteria. Protocols included theta/beta (n = 1), slow cortical potential (n = 1), alpha downregulation training (n = 1) and personalised approaches guided by individual alpha peak frequency (n = 3) or QEEG profiles (n = 1). Naturalistic and personalised studies reported large symptom reductions, whereas RCTs revealed small, generally non-significant effects relative to controls. Cognitive improvements were inconsistently reported and largely attributable to practice effects. Electrophysiological changes were protocol-specific without convergence across studies. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, small samples, variable controls, inconsistent learning metrics, and risk of bias. Current RCTs do not demonstrate evidence of efficacy over placebo. Blinded, adequately powered trials using standardised learning measures are needed to clarify mechanisms of neurofeedback.

papers.title: An incidental heterozygous ATP7B nonsense variant leading to a diagnostic pitfall for Wilson disease: a pediatric case report.
papers.abstract: Wilson disease (WD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in ATP7B, resulting in impaired copper transport and progressive copper accumulation, most prominently affecting the liver. With the growing use of genetic testing, incidental detection of ATP7B pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in individuals without typical hepatic phenotypes can prompt overdiagnosis and unnecessary investigations. This case highlights the importance of interpreting a single heterozygous ATP7B variant in the context of phenotype and a standardized biochemical diagnostic pathway for WD. A 13-year-old Han Chinese boy presented with recurrent brief paroxysmal attacks for > 1 year, markedly worsened over the preceding month. Episodes were triggered by rising from sitting, characterized by transient postural instability with unilateral head deviation and ipsilateral dystonic/choreiform movements, lasted ~ 10 s, and resolved spontaneously. Consciousness was preserved, with no incontinence, convulsions, or postictal symptoms. Interictal neurological examination was normal. Ambulatory EEG monitoring captured three typical attacks without epileptiform discharges or ictal EEG correlates, and brain MRI was unremarkable. A slit-lamp examination revealed no Kayser-Fleischer ring. A low serum copper level (9.43 µmol/L; reference 10.50-29.90) prompted further evaluation; genetic testing incidentally identified a heterozygous ATP7B variant (NM_000053.4:c.2851 C > T; p.Gln951Ter), reported as likely pathogenic. WD was considered. However, ceruloplasmin was normal (231.6 mg/L; reference 200.0-420.0 mg/L), ceruloplasmin oxidase activity measured by the p-phenylenediamine method was normal (0.372 OD; reference > 0.200 OD), liver biochemistry was normal (ALT 11 U/L, AST 16 U/L, GGT 14 U/L; bilirubin within reference range), and abdominal ultrasound showed a normal liver and biliary tree. Crucially, a follow-up quantitative 24-hour urinary copper test was strictly normal, and parental segregation analysis confirmed that the ATP7B variant represented a paternally inherited heterozygous state without biochemical evidence of Wilson disease, making active Wilson disease highly unlikely. This case illustrates a critical diagnostic pitfall: incidental heterozygous ATP7B variants can trigger severe diagnostic anchoring bias. To prevent overdiagnosis, genetic findings must be subordinated to strict phenotype-driven evaluations, formal Leipzig scoring, and definitive biochemical gold standards.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea is frequent in patients with Long COVID fatigue but is not significantly associated with alterations of quality of life and cognition.
papers.abstract: Neurologic manifestations of Long COVID, also called post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), include fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, sleep disturbances, and headaches, which can be debilitating. Since these symptoms overlap with those of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), we sought to determine the prevalence of OSA in the population of a Neuro-COVID-19 clinic. We performed home sleep testing in 100 consecutive patients with Long COVID and no prior history of OSA who reported fatigue after an episode of COVID-19 not requiring hospitalization. The average age was 46.4 years and 70% of patients were female. OSA was present in 53% of patients, including 33% with mild OSA (apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 5-14.9) and 20% with moderate to severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15). Male sex, higher age, and body mass index were significantly associated with OSA. However, there were no significant differences in other comorbidities, Long COVID symptom burden, quality of life measures (QoL), and objective cognitive function test results between groups. Additionally, multiple linear regression models demonstrated that neither AHI nor mean desaturation nadir were significant predictors of QoL or cognitive function. Although OSA is nearly twice as prevalent among our study participants compared to the general adult population of the US, it was not significantly associated with Long COVID symptoms, alteration of QoL, or objective cognitive dysfunction. However, 20% of patients were diagnosed with moderate to severe OSA, a clinically significant finding that warrants intervention to prevent irreversible cardiopulmonary complications.

papers.title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction.
papers.abstract: Understanding language in real-world interaction requires methods that integrate auditory, visual, and neural signals. We present a proof-of-concept study combining mobile electroencephalography (EEG) and eye tracking to investigate referential selection during dyadic communication. Using a simplified version of the director task, pairs of participants engaged in naturalistic object-movement instructions while EEG and gaze data were recorded and synchronized via LabStreamingLayer, allowing us to calculate overlap-corrected, regression-based event-related potentials (rERPs) time-locked to spoken nouns and to participants' fixations, focusing on the N400/P300 (300-500 ms) and later (500-800 ms) time windows. Our results show that gaze behavior and fixation-related potentials provide crucial information for interpreting language-related ERPs: Targets competing with occluded referents elicited a stronger posterior positivity consistent with greater attentional demands. Fixation timing systematically modulated neural responses. Contrary to predictions, competitors received little visual attention, indicating that participants prioritized task-relevant information. These findings highlight the potential of multimodal data integration for understanding attentional and predictive mechanisms in real-world communication. Importantly, we show that established analytic techniques, such as artifact subspace reconstruction, independent component analysis, and linear deconvolution for ERP calculation, apply to noisy, naturalistic datasets. In addition, we provide a subsampling sensitivity approach to test the stability of the effects across different sample sizes. This study provides a methodological framework linking gaze and neural activity during interactive language processing. All preprocessing and analysis scripts, along with example datasets, are openly available on OSF ( https://osf.io/5ds4z ; a modified and optimized Python implementation is also available on GitHub: https://github.com/XlinCLab/DGAME ).

papers.title: Construction and validation of a predictive model for sleep disorders among rural older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
papers.abstract: to construct and validate a risk assessment model for sleep disturbance among rural older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), to support early screening and targeted intervention. a cross-sectional study using data from the 2024 baseline survey of the Active Aging Cohort in Rural Areas, Shandong Province, China. 1,049 rural older adults aged ≥ 60 years with MCI. demographic, lifestyle, disease history, and psychological factors were collected through face-to-face survey questionnaires and health examinations. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Logistic regression identified independent predictors, which were used to build a nomogram. Model performance was evaluated with ROC curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation. the prevalence of sleep disturbance was 54.2%. Sex, hypertension, self-rated health, and depression were identified as independent predictors. The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination (AUC = 0.759, 95%CI: 0.731-0.778) and calibration, with internal validation confirming robustness.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: The mediating effects of adaptive coping and sleep quality in the relationship between trait emotional intelligence and trauma outcomes.
papers.abstract: Response to trauma varies from post-traumatic distress (PTS) to post-traumatic growth (PTG) seemingly depending on internal and external individual resources. This study examines the relationships among trait Emotional Intelligence (trait EI), sleep quality, adaptive coping, and differential outcomes of trauma, namely PTS and PTG, in adolescents exposed to collective chronic adversities, including the health pandemic and sociopolitical instability. This cross-sectional study involved 612 high school students (323 women) aged between 14 and 21 (M = 16.44, SD = 1.25) from Lebanese public schools. Measures assessed trait EI through the (TEI-QUE), adaptive coping (Brief-COPE), post-traumatic stress (PCL-5), sleep quality through the Sleep Quality Assessment, and post-traumatic growth (PTGI-SF). Structural equation modelling (SEM) was performed with robust estimators. Trait EI directly and indirectly associated with PTS and PTG. We found positive relationships between trait EI and adaptive coping (β = 0.58, p < .001) and trait EI and sleep quality (β = 0.37, p < .001), and between adaptive coping, and both PTS (β = 0.46, p < .001) and PTG (β = 0.43, p < .001). In addition, we found negative relationships between sleep and PTS (β = - 0.1, p < .05) and PTG (β = - 0.15, p < .001). The pathways involving adaptive coping and sleep quality were significantly associated with both PTS (β = 0.23, p < .001) and PTG (β = 0.19, p < .001), respectively, in relation to trait EI. Findings indicate that trauma outcomes are associated with trait EI, adaptive coping strategies, and sleep quality. The study advocates for the integration of these evidence-based cognitive and behavioral trainings in educational programs designed for adolescents in high-risk environments.

papers.title: Comment on "melatonin and oxidative DNA damage in REM- and NREM-related obstructive sleep apnea: an exploratory analysis of sleep-stage phenotypes".
